name: Nod and Roll
summary: The user looks at an object and nods to select it, while tilting the head left or right gives commands such as next and previous.
howItWorks: Eye gaze indicates the object of interest; because the vestibulo-ocular reflex keeps the eyes on it, the head is free to gesture. A nod (downward then upward head acceleration beyond an angular threshold within a time window) selects or activates the gazed object. Head rolls are recognised as roll-and-return, roll-and-stay, or left-then-right sequences, giving seven discrete commands in total (e.g. browsing a gallery of paintings). It was only tried informally (N=8): rated fun, though heavy HMDs made nodding awkward.
